::: {.ik-do}
**What you'll do**

1. Read what the hi-hats is.
2. Learn how it makes its sound.
3. Take a guided tour: press each **▶ Hear step** button and listen for one change.
4. Look up famous uses.
5. Check yourself with a short quiz.
:::

## What it is

- Two cymbals, 13-15", on a pedal stand: **open**, **closed** and **pedal** (foot) sounds (Wikipedia, "Hi-hat").

## How it sounds

- A cymbal has many long, **inharmonic** partials (unverified: no physics text read for this page). Bigger is louder and longer; heavier is louder with more cut (Wikipedia, "Cymbal").
- Closed: very short; open: long; the foot alone: the "chick".

"Cymbal." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cymbal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cymbal). Bigger: louder, longer sustain; heavier: louder, more cut; bell bronze the traditional alloy; B8 = 8 % tin malleable bronze, Paiste's "2002" alloy.

McLean, Scott, et al. "SM Drums (Deeply Sampled Free Drums)." SFZ edition, sfzinstruments, GitHub, accessed 27 Nov. 2026. The cymbal recordings the pages play (cymbal-samples/*.m4a). Its manual: "A Zildjian series" cymbals, 14" New Beat hats, 20" Ping and 17" Thin rides, 13/15/16/17" crashes, a Wuhan 15" china. Terms, the authors' site as quoted on KVR: free royalty free use by anyone for anything.

"Zildjian." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zildjian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zildjian). Founded Constantinople 1623; alloy recipe secret; K Zildjian made in the US from 1975, relaunched with Elvin Jones and Tony Williams.

**For students**

"Hi-hat." *Wikipedia*, Wikimedia Foundation, [en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hi-hat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hi-hat). Two 13-15" cymbals on a pedal stand; open, closed, pedal (foot) sounds.
:::
